steps.title: The calculator takes σ, not σ²
steps.body:
The IB writes a normal distribution as X ~ N(μ, σ²): the second number is the variance. Your calculator always asks for the standard deviation, σ.

steps.title: Properties of the curve
steps.body:
•  Symmetric about μ, so the mean, median and mode are all μ
•  The total area under the curve is 1
•  A single value has no area: P(X = a) = 0, so P(X < a) is the same as P(X ≤ a)
•  The tails never reach zero

steps.bad: ✗ Not quite. The false one is P(X = 170) = 0.5: a single value has no area, so its probability is 0.

steps.title: The 68–95–99.7 rule
steps.body:
Within one, two and three standard deviations of the mean:
•  68% lie within σ of μ
•  95% lie within 2σ
•  99.7% lie within 3σ

On Paper 1 this replaces the calculator: P(X > μ + σ) ≈ 0.16 and P(μ − 2σ < X < μ + 2σ) ≈ 0.95. Symmetry gives the rest: P(X < μ − a) = P(X > μ + a).

steps.bad: ✗ Not quite. 162 = μ − σ and 186 = μ + 2σ. Half of 68% (0.34) plus half of 95% (0.475) = 0.815.

hints: “Given that the wait is more than \(55\) s” shrinks the sample space to waits over \(55\). Use \(\mathrm{P}(A \mid B)=\dfrac{\mathrm{P}(A \cap B)}{\mathrm{P}(B)}\).
Here \(X>60\) and \(X>55\) together is just \(X>60\). So \(\mathrm{P}(X>60 \mid X>55)=\dfrac{\mathrm{P}(X>60)}{\mathrm{P}(X>55)}\): two normalCdf values, then one division.

fig.caption: Divide the tail beyond 60 (0.0478) by the tail beyond 55 (0.202).

parts: “Given that the wait is more than \(55\)”: which formula?
✓ Conditional probability divides by the probability of the condition.
✗ \(\mathrm{P}(A\mid B)=\dfrac{\mathrm{P}(A\cap B)}{\mathrm{P}(B)}\), and \(X>60\) and \(X>55\) together is just \(X>60\).
sets.name: C1 Conditional
sets.q: Given that a wait is more than \(55\) s, find the probability that it is more than \(60\) s.
sets.label: \(\mathrm{P}(X>60 \mid X>55)=\)
steps: \(X \sim \mathrm{N}(50,\,6^2)\). “Given that the wait is more than \(55\)” restricts us to waits over \(55\); inside that group we want the share over \(60\).
\(\mathrm{P}(X>60 \mid X>55)=\dfrac{\mathrm{P}(X>60 \cap X>55)}{\mathrm{P}(X>55)}=\dfrac{\mathrm{P}(X>60)}{\mathrm{P}(X>55)}\), because every wait over \(60\) is already over \(55\).
Two Normal Cdf calls with \(\mu=50\), \(\sigma=6\): Lower \(60\), Upper \(\infty\) gives \(0.0478\); Lower \(55\), Upper \(\infty\) gives \(0.2023\). Then divide.
\(\dfrac{0.0478}{0.2023}=0.236\). Check: the answer must be bigger than \(\mathrm{P}(X>60)=0.0478\) alone, because the condition shrinks the sample space.
wrongs: \(0.0478\) is \(\mathrm{P}(X>60)\) alone. “Given that” means divide by \(\mathrm{P}(X>55)\).
\(0.202\) is \(\mathrm{P}(X>55)\), the denominator. Divide \(\mathrm{P}(X>60)\) by it.
\(0.0097\) is the product. Conditional probability divides; it does not multiply.

hints: Conditional: divide by the probability of the condition, \(\mathrm{P}(X>85)\).

fig.caption: Divide the tail beyond 90 (0.106) by the tail beyond 85 (0.266).

parts: Given a score over \(85\), probability it is over \(90\): which formula?
sets.name: C1 Conditional
sets.q: Given that a score is more than \(85\), find the probability that it is more than \(90\).
sets.label: \(\mathrm{P}(X>90 \mid X>85)=\)
steps: \(X \sim \mathrm{N}(80,\,8^2)\). Given a score over \(85\), we want the share over \(90\).
Two Normal Cdf calls with \(\mu=80\), \(\sigma=8\): Lower \(90\) gives \(0.1056\); Lower \(85\) gives \(0.2660\). Divide.
\(\dfrac{0.1056}{0.2660}=0.397\). Check: larger than \(\mathrm{P}(X>90)\) alone, as a conditional probability over a smaller group must be.
wrongs: \(0.106\) is \(\mathrm{P}(X>90)\) alone. Divide by \(\mathrm{P}(X>85)\).
\(0.266\) is the denominator.
\(0.0281\) is the product. Divide, not multiply.

steps: \(X \sim \mathrm{N}(45,\,6^2)\); two independent journeys both over \(55\) minutes.
Normal Cdf with Lower \(=55\), Upper \(=\infty\), \(\mu=45\), \(\sigma=6\) gives \(0.04779\). Square it.

sets.name: C4 In terms of σ
sets.q: Find the probability that \(X\) is more than \(2\) standard deviations from the mean.
sets.label: \(\mathrm{P}(|X-\mu|>2\sigma)=\)
steps: “More than \(2\) standard deviations from the mean” is two tails: below \(\mu-2\sigma\) and above \(\mu+2\sigma\).
With \(\mu=0\), \(\sigma=1\): Normal Cdf Lower \(=-\infty\), Upper \(=-2\) gives \(0.0228\). Double it.
\(2\times0.0228=0.0455\). Check: \(95\%\) lies within \(2\sigma\), so about \(5\%\) lies outside.
wrongs: \(0.0228\) is one tail. Double it.
\(0.954\) is within \(2\sigma\). The question asks for outside.

questions.stem: The masses of apples grown on a farm are normally distributed with mean \(165\) g and standard deviation \(12\) g. An apple is chosen at random.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the probability that the apple has a mass less than \(150\) g.
parts.figCap: Shade the left tail below 150: z = (150 − 165)/12 = −1.25.
ms: \(X \sim \mathrm{N}(165,\,12^{2})\); \(\mathrm{P}(X<150)\) written, or a sketch with the left tail shaded
wrongs: \(0.894\) is \(\mathrm{P}(X>150)\): the wrong tail.
\(0.227\) uses \(\sigma=20\) or a typing slip; \(\sigma=12\).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Find the probability that the apple has a mass between \(150\) g and \(180\) g.
parts.figCap: The middle band from 150 to 180; both bounds typed into Normal Cdf.
ms: \(\mathrm{P}(150<X<180)\), or Normal Cdf with bounds \(150\) and \(180\)
wrongs: \(0.894\) is \(\mathrm{P}(X>150)\): the upper bound \(180\) was left off.
That is part (a).
\(0.211\) is \(1-0.789\): the two tails together.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: The farm packs \(200\) apples. Find the expected number of apples with a mass greater than \(180\) g.
parts.figCap: Right tail above 180, then multiply the probability by 200.
parts.note: Expected number \(=n\times p\). Do not round \(p\) before multiplying; \(200\times0.11=22\) loses the accuracy mark.
wrongs: That is the probability for one apple; multiply by \(200\).
\(22\) comes from rounding \(p\) to \(0.11\) first. Keep the full value: \(21.1\).
\(179\) is the expected number \(\le180\) g; the question says greater than.

questions.stem: The reaction times of adults, in milliseconds, are modelled by \(T \sim \mathrm{N}(120,\,15^{2})\).

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Write down the probability that a reaction time is less than \(120\) ms.
parts.figCap: Half the area lies below the mean: no calculator needed.
ms: \(0.5\): \(120\) is the mean, and the distribution is symmetric
parts.note: “Write down” means no working is expected: the mean splits the area in half.
wrongs: The mean is \(120\): exactly half the area lies below it.
That is the mean itself; the probability is \(0.5\).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: Find the probability that a reaction time is more than \(140\) ms.
wrongs: \(0.909\) is \(\mathrm{P}(T<140)\): the wrong tail.

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: Given that a reaction time is more than \(140\) ms, find the probability that it is more than \(150\) ms.
parts.figCap: The darker region (T > 150) sits inside the lighter one (T > 140): divide the smaller area by the larger.
parts.note: Follow-through: with your own value of \(\mathrm{P}(T>140)\) in the denominator, a correct method still earns the marks.
wrongs: \(0.0228\) is \(\mathrm{P}(T>150)\) alone; divide by \(\mathrm{P}(T>140)\).
\(0.0021\) multiplied the two probabilities; a condition divides.
The fraction is upside down: \(\mathrm{P}(T>150)\) on top.

parts.label: (d)

parts.figCap: Within 20 of the mean is the band 100 < T < 140.
wrongs: That is one tail; “within \(20\)” is the middle band \(100<T<140\).
\(0.909\) is \(\mathrm{P}(T<140)\): the lower bound \(100\) was left off.
\(0.182\) is the two tails together; the question wants the middle.

questions.stem: A machine fills bags of sugar. The mass, \(M\) grams, of a bag is normally distributed with mean \(500\) and standard deviation \(12\). A bag is rejected if its mass is less than \(480\) g.

parts.label: (a)
parts.text: Find the probability that a randomly chosen bag is rejected.
parts.figCap: Rejected bags: the left tail below 480 (z = −1.67).
wrongs: The wrong tail: rejected means less than \(480\).

parts.label: (b)
parts.text: A bag is chosen at random and is not rejected. Find the probability that its mass is more than \(520\) g.
parts.figCap: Condition “not rejected” is everything from 480 up; the event M > 520 is the darker tail inside it.
parts.note: The condition “not rejected” restricts to \(M\ge480\): divide by \(1-\) part (a). Follow-through applies to your part (a) value.
wrongs: \(0.0478\) is \(\mathrm{P}(M>520)\) alone; divide by \(\mathrm{P}(M\ge480)=0.952\).
\(0.0455\) multiplied by \(0.952\); a condition divides.
That is the denominator, \(\mathrm{P}(M\ge480)\).

parts.label: (c)
parts.text: The machine is adjusted so that the mean changes but the standard deviation stays \(12\) g. After the adjustment, only \(1\%\) of bags are rejected. Find the new mean.
parts.figCap: Only 1% below 480 means 480 sits 2.33σ below the new mean: μ = 480 + 2.3263 × 12.
parts.note: Two of the four marks are for the \(z\)-value and the standardising equation: write them, even though the GDC did the arithmetic.
wrongs: \(492\) used \(z=+2.33\): \(480\) must be below the mean, so \(z\) is negative and \(\mu>480\).
\(500\) is the old mean; it has to move up so that fewer bags fall under \(480\).
That is \(|z|\); the question asks for \(\mu\).
